title: CPR
subtitle: Cardiac emergency
warning: Use an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) as soon as one is available.
steps: Check for responsiveness and normal breathing.
Call emergency services (112 or 108) or ask someone nearby to do so immediately.
Place heel of one hand in center of chest, other hand on top with interlocking fingers.
Deliver hard, fast compressions at a rate of 100–120 per minute at 5–6 cm depth.
Continue chest compressions continuously until emergency responders take over or AED prompts.

title: Choking
subtitle: Blocked airway
warning: If the person becomes unresponsive, lower them to the ground and begin chest compressions (CPR).
steps: Ask 'Are you choking?' and check if the person can speak, cough, or breathe.
Lean the person slightly forward and deliver 5 firm back blows between shoulder blades with heel of hand.
If airway remains blocked, give 5 quick upward abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) just above navel.
Alternate between 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until object is expelled.
For infants under 1 year, alternate 5 back slaps with 2-finger chest thrusts only.

title: Severe Bleeding
subtitle: Severe wound care
warning: Do not remove embedded objects or peel off soaked initial dressings.
steps: Protect yourself with clean gloves or a waterproof barrier if available.
Apply firm, continuous direct pressure with sterile gauze or clean cloth directly over wound.
Keep pressure constant for at least 5 minutes; layer additional pads if blood soaks through.
Elevate the injured limb above heart level only if no broken bones are suspected.
If severe bleeding continues on a limb, apply a commercial tourniquet 5–7 cm above the wound.

title: Burns
subtitle: Heat or chemical injury
warning: Never apply ice, butter, oils, toothpaste, or adhesive dressings to burns.
steps: Ensure personal safety, remove heat source, and gently take off hot non-adherent clothing.
Cool the burn under clean, cool running water for at least 20 minutes.
Carefully remove rings, watches, or restrictive clothing before swelling develops.
Loosely cover burned skin with sterile non-stick dressing or clean plastic wrap.
Seek emergency hospital treatment immediately for deep, chemical, electrical, or extensive burns.

title: Fractures & Sprains
subtitle: Bone and joint injury
warning: Never attempt to straighten a deformed limb or push an exposed bone back in.
steps: Instruct the injured person to remain completely still and support the injured limb in place.
Control any open bleeding with gentle pressure around the wound, avoiding bone pressure.
Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth for 15–20 minutes at a time to reduce swelling.
Splint the joint above and below the fracture only if transport is unavoidable and you are trained.
Check frequently for pulse, warmth, and sensation beyond the injured area.

title: Seizures
subtitle: Protect and monitor
warning: Do not restrain the person, and never place fingers, spoons, or objects into their mouth.
steps: Guide the person safely away from hard edges, traffic, water, and sharp objects.
Place a folded jacket or soft cushion under their head to protect from impact trauma.
Note the start time of the seizure and gently loosen tight collars, ties, or neckwear.
Once active convulsions cease, roll the person onto their side into recovery position to clear airway.
Stay calmly beside them until fully alert; call 112 if seizure lasts over 5 minutes or repeats.

title: Heatstroke
subtitle: Dangerous overheating
warning: Heatstroke is a medical emergency. Rapid whole-body cooling takes priority.
steps: Move the patient immediately into dense shade or an air-conditioned room/vehicle.
Remove heavy outer clothing to expose as much skin as possible.
Immerse in cold water, or spray continuous cool water while actively fanning their skin.
Apply ice packs or cold wet towels to armpits, groin, neck, and back.
Never force fluids if patient is confused, drowsy, or unconscious.

title: Snake Bite
subtitle: Venomous puncture injury
warning: Do NOT cut the wound, suck out venom, apply ice, or tie a tight arterial tourniquet.
steps: Keep the patient calm and completely still; physical movement accelerates venom circulation.
Remove rings, bangles, anklets, and shoes before rapid limb swelling occurs.
Immobilize the bitten limb at or slightly below heart level with a splint.
Apply a firm crepe bandage starting from fingers/toes up the limb if trained in pressure immobilization.
Transport immediately to the nearest hospital with Anti-Snake Venom (ASV) availability.

title: Shock & Hypothermia
subtitle: Low perfusion & extreme cold
warning: Do not apply direct intense heat (radiators, hot water) which can cause cardiovascular collapse.
steps: Lay the person flat and elevate their legs 20–30 cm unless head, neck, or spinal injury is suspected.
Remove damp, cold clothing gently and replace with warm, dry blankets or emergency thermal foil.
Insulate the patient from cold ground using a sleeping mat, coats, or tarp underneath.
Cover their head and neck while keeping face exposed to preserve core body heat.
Offer warm sweet non-caffeinated drinks only if the patient is fully conscious and swallowing easily.

title: Poisoning & Ingestion
subtitle: Toxic substance exposure
warning: Do not induce vomiting unless specifically instructed by a medical toxicologist.
steps: Identify the toxic chemical, plant, pesticide, or medication container if safe to do so.
If the substance is on skin or eyes, irrigate copiously with clean running water for 15–20 minutes.
If toxic gas or fumes were inhaled, bring victim into fresh open air immediately.
Place an unconscious breathing victim into the lateral recovery position.
Call National Poison Information Centre (1800-116-117) or 112 immediately with product details.
